title: French Revolution
examples: What were the main reasons for the French Revolution?
How did the revolution change France?
What was Napoleon's role after the revolution?

explain.say: The French Revolution had many causes building up over time.
The old social system had three main groups called estates.
A concrete example is that the Third Estate paid most of the taxes.

draw.text: Taxes paid by the Third Estate

explain.say: The revolution went through several distinct stages of change.
Napoleon Bonaparte rose to power after the initial revolutionary period ended.
In everyday life, a disagreement over fairness can cause big changes.

faq.q: Why did the revolution become so radical?
faq.a: The initial moderate changes were often blocked by powerful groups. The increasing violence and fear fueled more extreme actions.
asks: What made the revolution more radical?
Why did things get so violent?

faq.q: What was the main problem with the old French government?
faq.a: The system was unfair because the wealthy estates paid taxes while the poor bore the burden. This created deep resentment.
asks: What was wrong with the King's rule?

faq.a: He was a successful general who rose through the ranks during the chaos. He eventually took control of France, changing its structure.
asks: What did Napoleon do after the revolution?

faq.q: What did the Enlightenment ideas teach people?
faq.a: These ideas emphasized natural rights and the power of the people. They challenged the divine right of kings.
asks: What did the thinkers say about government?
What new ideas spread through France?

faq.q: Did the revolution end with Napoleon?
faq.a: No, Napoleon's rule eventually collapsed, leading to further changes in French governance over time.
asks: Was the revolution finished after he ruled?

facts: The Enlightenment emphasized reason and individual rights.
The Three Estates system was a major source of social tension.
The storming of the Bastille symbolized the start of the revolution.
Napoleon established himself as Emperor of the French.

quiz.say: The primary reason for the social unrest before the revolution was:
quiz.show: Tax burden on the Third Estate

options.show: The unfair tax system where the Third Estate paid most taxes.
options.say: The unfair tax system where the Third Estate paid most taxes.

options.show: The King wanting too much money.
options.say: The King wanting too much money.

quiz.why: This directly relates to the social inequality that fueled the uprising.

wrong.0: External threats were factors, but the internal social structure was the main cause.
wrong.2: The Enlightenment ideas actually gave people the reason to protest the unfairness.
wrong.3: While money was an issue, the system of unfair payments was the core problem.

quiz.say: Which event marks the beginning of the revolution?
quiz.why: This event is historically recognized as the symbolic start of the violent upheaval.

wrong.0: This happened much later and was an outcome, not the beginning.
wrong.1: Writing ideas was a cause, but the physical storming was the action.
wrong.2: The King's actions were part of the process, but the people's action started it.

quiz.say: Napoleon's main achievement after the revolution was:

options.show: Returning France to the old monarchy.
options.say: Returning France to the old monarchy.

options.show: Restoring the power of the clergy.
options.say: Restoring the power of the clergy.

quiz.why: He moved from a general to a ruler who reorganized French law and governance.

wrong.0: He overthrew the monarchy, even if he later adopted some royal titles.
wrong.1: His rule caused new conflicts across Europe.
wrong.2: The revolution significantly reduced the power of the Church.
